statusText: Green. The weekend CME halt continues with no live Nasdaq-100 price path; Tail rests at the low-band floor and the mapped policy state is EA_ON.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Tail remains far below the block threshold. One narrow observation window is flagged across the 22:00-23:30 UTC Sunday futures reopen, where September rate pricing that is still split across venues meets thin initial liquidity and two-way gap risk. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100: a halted market holds tail risk at the low-band floor while September rate pricing stays split across venues
body:
This assessment falls inside the weekend CME halt, so no live NQ price path exists and no mean-reversion failure can be developing. The anchor is Friday's completed session, re-verified against the Nasdaq-100 quote page this hour: the index opened 29,545.90, reached 29,752.78, fell to 29,383.92 and closed 29,433.43, down 0.70% from a 29,641.56 previous close. That leaves the close roughly 50 points off the low of a 369-point range, a downside reversal inside a finished session. The Nasdaq Composite nevertheless ended the week 0.9% higher at 26,402.42 and the S&P 500 closed 7,711.76 for a 0.5% weekly gain, so Friday reads as rotation rather than an extending trend. VIX closed 14.43 inside a 14.13-14.84 range and carried no volatility premium into the weekend.

The refinement this hour is that September rate pricing is not a single number. Fed funds futures imply roughly 56-57% odds of a 25bp hike, up from about 35% before the Jackson Hole keynote, while Kalshi and Polymarket price the same decision nearer 47-49%. A spread of that size between the futures curve and prediction markets is an uncertainty signal: it says the market has not converged on the September path rather than that a directional repricing is complete. On the inherited framework that lifts Stress and Confidence considerations, not Tail, because no live index path has tested any of it.

The internal composition remains narrow. Every tracked semiconductor closed lower, with ARM near -6.3%, NVDA near -4.6% and INTC near -2.9%, while five of eight megacaps rose and the Communication Services and Consumer Cyclical sectors gained. Technology fell about 1.4% against a 1.4% gain in Communication Services. Divergent internals of that kind reduce directional conviction; they do not mechanically amplify Tail. The shared cross-asset context file is past its freshness window this hour, so it is used only as static colour on a session that has already closed, and the assessment rests on independently verified primary sources.

H.15 shows the 2-year at 4.20%, the 10-year at 4.67% and the 30-year at 5.19% as of 27 August. Cross-asset behaviour is only partly aligned: gold near 4,600 dollars fell about 2.9% on Friday while still tracking its biggest monthly gain since 1999, and WTI near 83.44 dollars extended weekly losses to roughly 4% as Persian Gulf exports recovered to 15-16 million barrels a day and an Iran-Oman corridor framework reduced perceived supply risk. Iran's deputy foreign minister restated on Saturday that the strait remains closed and that transits occur in coordination with Tehran, which repeats a known position rather than opening a new market channel.

One narrow observation window is flagged across the 22:00-23:30 UTC Sunday reopen, where carried rate pricing meets thin initial liquidity and two-way gap risk. The week that follows is a known catalyst stack rather than a surprise: ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on Tuesday, ADP and the Beige Book on Wednesday, ISM Services on Thursday, Broadcom after Wednesday's close, and August payrolls on Friday. A known calendar informs Stress and Confidence; it is not evidence of a pathological price path. Tail therefore rests at the low-band floor and the mapped policy state is EA_ON.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, covering the weekend halt from Saturday evening through the hour before this one. The series was uniformly green with Tail fixed at 5, dominant mode normal and Stress confined to a 25-27 band. Confidence decayed from 69 to 58 as published evidence aged across the closed market, then recovered through 64 and 72 to 81 as primary sources were re-verified on each refresh. No hour in the window contained an observable NQ price path.
outlookSummary: The next six projected hours remain inside the weekend CME halt, where no price path can form; Tail stays at the low-band floor of 5 while Stress drifts from 27 to 29 into the reopen and Confidence decays from 82 to 77 with ageing evidence. From the projected 22:00 UTC reopen the conditional Tail lifts to 12, still inside the low band and well below the block threshold, covering the first live test of a September rate path that futures and prediction markets currently price differently. It then eases through 11 and 10 across the Asian session to an overnight low of 8, recovers to 9 through European hours, and steps up to a projected peak of 14 in the hour containing Monday's 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open before easing through 13 for the Dallas Fed Manufacturing release and 12 at the edge of the horizon. Every projected hour maps to EA_ON; all of it is conditional, since no structure after this assessment has been observed.
